scope: Offline FakeVenue, VirtualClock, file SQLite. No live accounts or server restart.

20Windows.limitations: Timed ticks use normal GC and include writer contention. Normal-GC steady RSS uses 20 x 200 fixed-ledger ticks; last 5 windows must have range <=4MiB and positive slope <=0.25MiB/window, otherwise gate fails as unverified. The <=32MiB increment gate uses maxima of these last 5 normal-GC windows. Post-GC samples are diagnostic only. Timed RSS maxima are sampled every 100 ticks, not true process peaks. RSS includes workers. Finite tests cannot prove absence of all future growth; bounded queue/cache and repeated-batch regression provide structural evidence. No live latency/exposure improvement claim.

The <=32MiB increment gate uses maxima of these last 5 normal-GC windows. Post-GC samples are diagnostic only. Timed RSS maxima are sampled every 100 ticks, not true process peaks. measurementRaw.limitations: Timed ticks use normal GC and include writer contention. Normal-GC RSS runs 160 x 200 fixed-ledger ticks. Predeclared checkpoints 80/120/160 use the last 10 windows: both configurations require range <=4MiB and positive OLS slope <=0.25MiB/window. Use ONLY the first jointly stable checkpoint, independently of RSS increment; no joint stability means unverified/fail. The <=32MiB gate compares maxima of those windows. Post-GC samples are diagnostic only. Timed RSS maxima are sampled every 100 ticks, not true process peaks. RSS includes workers. Finite tests cannot prove absence of all future growth; bounded queue/cache and repeated-batch regression provide structural evidence. No live latency/exposure improvement claim.

analysisRule: vetoLaterGrowth can only add failures: every observed checkpoint at or after the selected one must be stable.

storeIsolation.method: Fixed 121-order in-memory Store after identical warmup; no observation and no FakeVenue calls during measurements; normal GC until final diagnostics.

storeIsolationSourceNote: Reproduction script normalizes the module path to repository cwd and writes JSON to stdout; the measured script used the same workload with an absolute local path and wrote the captured JSON to /tmp.
